name: hikari-1ae003c7-blind20-v2-ots
instr:
# hikari: nineteen undocumented behaviour regressions to diagnose without a test suite

A bot written on top of this library talks to a chat service: it takes in what the service pushes at it, keeps a local copy of some of that state, and assembles the requests it sends back. Since upgrading, a lot of small things across it answer questions backwards or drop data. The repository has received 19 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I have been able to pin down by poking at it from the outside.

Handling what the service pushes at us. For a freshly arrived message, the two convenience flags about where it came from are both exactly the wrong way round with respect to whether it carries the marker identifying it as machine-posted: one that has that marker is reported as not machine-posted, and one without it is reported as machine-posted. The companion flag is reversed against the same marker: a message with no such marker and an ordinary non-bot author is reported as not coming from a person, while a machine-posted one with a non-bot author is reported as coming from a person. Asking a "every mark of one symbol was cleared" notice whether it concerns a particular symbol gives the opposite answer for standard pictorial characters — passing the very symbol the notice is about returns false, and passing an unrelated one returns true — and a notice that is about an uploaded custom symbol (it has an id and no name) also claims to be about an arbitrary standard character
